sections.html:
Middletown is a Middlesex County city on the west bank of the Connecticut River, about 16 miles south of Hartford. It had 47,717 residents in 2020 and covers 42.36 square miles. Of 21,671 housing units counted that year, 54% were owner-occupied. Route 9 runs beside the river and splits the city, and Interstate 91 clips only the western edge.

The river shaped the housing. Floods hit in 1927 and 1936, the Great New England Hurricane struck in 1938, and a highway built in the 1950s later cut the city off from the water. Older riverside neighborhoods carry that history, so a seller near the water should expect questions about flooding and drainage.

sections.h2: Mill rates and how the tax is figured
sections.html:
The Assessor values property at 70% of its value, and the city multiplies that assessment by the mill rate. For the October 1, 2025 grand list, with bills effective July 1, 2026, the combined real estate rate depends on which fire district the house is in. The city's mill rates page has the current numbers.

Fire districtCity mill rateDistrict rateCombined real estate rate
City Fire District33.307.5040.800
South Fire District33.305.31138.611
Westfield Fire District33.302.08435.384

The registered vehicle rate is capped at 32.46. The City Fire District tax is added to the city bill, but the South Fire and Westfield Fire Districts bill and collect on their own. An owner in either of those two should expect two bills.

sections.h2: Due dates, interest and who gets the bill
sections.html:
The tax year runs July 1 through June 30, with installments due July 1 and January 1. An installment not paid by the first business day of the following month carries interest at 1.5% per month, or 18% per year, from its due date. The Tax Collector's tax information page explains the rest.

  • Not getting a bill does not cancel the tax or the interest, and copies are free.
  • Banks and mortgage companies that escrow must request bills each year from the Tax Collector.
  • Bills go to the record owner as of the October 1 grand list date, and by law that name stays on the bill until the next assessment date.
  • If you pay off a mortgage, tell the office so it can update its records.

After a sale, the bill can therefore still carry the earlier owner's name, so confirm with the collector who receives it.

sections.h2: Selling a Middletown house with tax owed
sections.html:
Ask the Tax Collector for a payoff, and let the title company pay it from your proceeds at closing. Nothing has to come out of your pocket first. These steps keep it orderly.

  1. Find out which district your house is in, because the district decides how many bills you have.
  2. If the house is in the South Fire or Westfield Fire District, ask that district for its own balance too.
  3. Check whether a mortgage servicer still receives the bill, and tell the office if the loan has been paid off.
  4. Give every figure to your closing attorney in writing.

Bring the deed, a photo ID and, for an estate, the papers that name who can sign. The Middletown town clerk records the deed.

Middletown has three fire districts, and your house falls in exactly one of them. The city rate of 33.30 is identical across all three; only the fire district piece differs, from 7.50 in the City Fire District down to 5.311 in the South Fire District and 2.084 in the Westfield Fire District. That spread is why two houses with the same assessment can see different tax bills. A buyer comparing two listings will notice, so know your district before you advertise.

If you cannot tell which district applies, ask the Assessor or the Tax Collector, who can confirm it from the parcel. Owners in the South Fire and Westfield Fire Districts should also keep the district's own bill separate from the city bill, because paying one does not satisfy the other.

sections.h2: Mortgages, escrow and the record owner
sections.html:
Many Middletown bills go to a bank. Lenders that escrow are required to request each year's bills from the Tax Collector, so when you pay off a mortgage, call the office so the bill does not keep going to a servicer that no longer cares. Because the record owner on the October 1 grand list date stays on the bill until the next assessment date, a house sold in the middle of a year can still produce a bill in the previous owner's name. That is normal, but it creates confusion. Settle at closing who will pay the next installment, and put the answer in the closing paperwork.

When a bill never shows up, do not wait. Interest and the tax itself remain due, and free copies are available from the office. Ask for one, check the account number, and pay or arrange payment before the first business day of the following month.

The state conveyance tax return, Form OP-236, is filed when the deed is recorded, and Middletown's code on the Department of Revenue Services list is 083. The state page lists exemptions for a principal residence given in lieu of foreclosure and for one whose price does not cover the mortgages plus the priority tax liens.

If you are selling an inherited house, the probate court district covers Middletown along with Cromwell, Portland, Middlefield and Haddam. The estate needs someone authorized before a deed can be signed, so start that process before you look for a buyer. Ask the Tax Collector to send bills to that person while the estate is open.

Middletown sellers come in a few kinds: owners behind on tax, heirs to a house they do not want, and owners who live somewhere else. Cash Home Buyers buys Middletown houses as-is in each of those cases. You skip repairs and showings, and the title company settles what is owed from the proceeds. Whether that beats listing depends on how much work the house needs and how long you can carry it.

faqs.q: When are Middletown real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: July 1 and January 1. Interest of 1.5% per month applies if an installment is not paid by the first business day of the following month.
The Assessor values property at 70% of its value, and the city multiplies that assessment by the mill rate.

faqs.q: What is the Middletown mill rate?
faqs.a: For the October 1, 2025 grand list, the combined real estate rate is 40.800 mills in the City Fire District, 38.611 in the South Fire District and 35.384 in the Westfield Fire District.

faqs.q: Do some Middletown owners get two tax bills?
faqs.a: Yes. South Fire and Westfield Fire District owners are billed by those districts separately from the city.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Middletown house if I owe tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The title company normally pays the tax from your sale proceeds at closing.
